questions.text: Register map: give the offset, width, reset value and access of every register the test shell exposes (ID, CRC readback, CLEAR control, DATA input).
questions.default: ID at 0x00 RO reset 0x43524333; CRC at 0x04 RO reset 0x00000000; CTRL at 0x08 WO with bit 0 CLEAR; DATA at 0x0C WO with 32-bit word
questions.reason: spec.md says the CRC is read back and cleared over the UART shell and names the ID, so the proposed map is kept until the shell map is confirmed
questions.answer: ID at 0x00 RO reset 0x43524333; CRC at 0x04 RO reset 0x00000000; CTRL at 0x08 WO with bit 0 CLEAR; DATA at 0x0C WO with 32-bit word

questions.text: Bit and byte order of a data word: which bit and which byte enter the CRC first?
questions.default: least significant bit first within each byte, bytes from bits 7:0 to 31:24 (little endian), the usual Ethernet byte order
questions.reason: the reflected CRC-32 is defined over a byte stream, and the word-to-stream order decides the result
questions.answer: least significant bit first within each byte, bytes from bits 7:0 to 31:24 (little endian), the usual Ethernet byte order

questions.text: Should the CRC register read the finalised value (state XOR 0xFFFFFFFF) or the raw running state?
questions.default: finalised value, so the empty stream reads 0x00000000 and the 123456789 check value is 0xCBF43926
questions.reason: spec.md says standard Ethernet CRC-32, which includes the final XOR, and a checker needs the standard check value
questions.answer: finalised value, so the empty stream reads 0x00000000 and the 123456789 check value is 0xCBF43926

questions.text: When CLEAR and a DATA write occur in the same clock, which wins?
questions.default: CLEAR wins and the data word is dropped
questions.reason: a clear is a reset-like command, and dropping the word keeps the state well defined in one cycle
questions.answer: CLEAR wins and the data word is dropped

questions.text: Is the UART baud rate and frame format (8N1 at 115200 baud) fixed by the existing shell?
questions.default: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit
questions.reason: spec.md does not give the baud rate; 115200 8N1 is the common default for the Nexys A7 USB-UART bridge
questions.answer: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit

questions.text: Should the LEDs show the CRC low 16 bits when reset is active?
questions.default: yes, they show 0x0000 during and after reset because the CRC register reads 0x00000000 then
questions.reason: spec.md says the LEDs show the low 16 bits of the CRC and gives no reset behaviour for them
questions.answer: yes, they show 0x0000 during and after reset because the CRC register reads 0x00000000 then
